layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One of the most common modalities to examine the human eye is the eye-fundus photograph. The evaluation of fundus photographs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is carried out by medical experts during time-consuming visual inspection. Our aim is to accelerate this process using computer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aided diagnosis. As a first step, it is necessary to segment structures in the images for tissue differentiation. As the eye is the only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: organ, where the vasculature can be imaged in an in vivo and noninterventional way without using expensive scanners, the vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tree is one of the most interesting and important structures to analyze. The quality and resolution of fundus images are rapidly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing. Thus, segmentation methods need to be adapted to the new challenges of high resolutions. In this paper, we present a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method to reduce calculation time, achieve high accuracy, and increase sensitivity compared to the original Frangi method. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method contains approaches to avoid potential problems like specular reflexes of thick vessels. The proposed method is evaluated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the STARE and DRIVE databases and we propose a new high resolution fundus database to compare it to the state-of-the-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: art algorithms. The results show an average accuracy above 94% and low computational needs. This outperforms state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In ophthalmology the most common way to examine the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: human eye is to take an eye-fundus photograph and to anal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yse it. During this kind of eye examinations a medical expert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acquires a photo of the eye-background through the pupil

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a fundus camera. The analysis of these images is comm-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only done by visual inspection. This process can require hours

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in front of a computer screen, in particular in case of medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screening. An example fundus image is shown in Figure 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our goal is to speed up the diagnosis by processing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images using computer algorithms to find and highlight the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most important details. In addition we aim to automatically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: identify abnormalities and diseases with minimal human

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interaction. Due to the rapidly increasing spatial resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of fundus images, the common image processing methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which were developed and tested using low resolution images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have shown drawbacks in clinical use. For this purpose, a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation of methods needs to be developed. These methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: need to be able to operate on high resolution images with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low computational complexity. In this paper, we would like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to introduce a novel vessel segmentation method with low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational needs and a public available high resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fundus database with manually generated gold standards for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation of retinal structure segmentation methods. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed algorithms include modifications to the method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed by Frangi et al. [1] to decrease the running time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and to segment specular reflexes of thick vessels, which are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not visible in lower resolution fundus images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The structure of the paper is as follows. We describe the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed methods in detail in Section 3. In Section 4, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present the evaluation methods and databases, including our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed high resolution fundus database, while Section 5

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presents the quantitative results. In Sections 6 and 7, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational complexity and robustness of the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithm are analyzed. This is followed by a Discussion in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 8 and the Conclusions in Section 9.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Retinal vessel segmentation is a challenging task and has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been in the focus of researches all over the world for years.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During this time many different algorithms were published

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [2]. The segmentation algorithms can be classified into two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: main groups: in unsupervised and supervised methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unsupervised methods classify vessels using heuristics, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised methods learn a criteria system automatically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using prelabeled data as gold standard. We focus on heuristic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods, as supervised methods need a large training set for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each camera setup. Heuristic methods instead require a set of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, which need to be adapted to the camera setup.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus, they are much more independent from the test dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during their development. A more detailed review of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation and other retinal image processing algorithms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be found in the articles published by Kirbas and Quek [2]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Patton et al. [3].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Early, but one of the most common approaches for fundus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images are the matched-filter approaches. One of the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods was presented by Chaudhuri et al. [4]. It fits pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defined vessel profiles with different sizes and orientations to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the image to enhance vessels. Similar methods and improve-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments were published later on by different authors [5-8].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Early implementations of these methods were using a simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding step to obtain a vessel segmentation. Sometimes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods were combined with other approaches [9–12].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, Zhang et al. [12] combined matched filters with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a method based on the Hessian matrix [1]. The matched filters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide high quality results, but the main disadvantage of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods is their requirement for vessel profiles and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparisons of large regions for each pixel in the image,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in long computational time. The quality of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation results heavily depends on the quality and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size of the used vessel profile database. This can be specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: towards ethnicity, camera setup, or even eye or vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diseases, which reduces its applicability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Some of the algorithms are specialized to segment only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one or more objects, which are marked by a user or in a pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing step. These methods are usually not analyzing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the whole image but the neighborhood of the already

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmented regions. Region growing [13, 14] and tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithms [15-18] are good examples for such kind of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation methods. The region-growing approaches are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trying to increase the segmented area with nearby pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on similarities and other criteria. These methods are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one of the fastest approaches, while they may have problems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at specific regions of the image, where the vessels have lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast compared to the nearby tissues, for example, vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: endings or thin vessels. In this case the region growing can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segment large unwanted areas. Vessel tracking algorithms are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more robust in those situations. They try to find a vessel-like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure in the already segmented region and track the given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels. 'These algorithms can recognize vessel endings much

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: easier, but they may have difficulties at bifurcations and vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crossings, where the local structures do not look like usual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels anymore. Hunter et al. [17] published a postprocessing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: step to solve some of these situations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Other common segmentation approaches are model-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based methods. The most known and commonly used ones

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are active contour-based methods, level-sets, and the so-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: called snakes [19]. The early snake-based algorithms start

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with an initial rough contour of the object, which is iteratively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refined driven by multiple forces. In an optimal case, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forces reach their equilibrium exactly on the object bound-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aries. These methods are sensitive to their parameterization,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while they may have problems if they have to segment thick

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and thin vessels in the same time. Thus, the parameters have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be set and refined manually by the user. The snakes in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this form are mostly used in MR [20] or X-ray angiographic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images [21] to segment pathologies and organs. The snake-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based retinal vessel segmentation methods usually apply a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel tracking framework to find the edges or the centerline

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the vessels and track them using snakes [17, 22, 23]. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: way the snakes are used to track only a vessel edge and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithm has less problems with vessel endings and differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent vessel thicknesses. Thus, their parameters are easier to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimize, but they inherit the problems of tracking algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithms with bifurcations and crossings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Level-set methods provide a more robust solution than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: snakes. They are usually used in combination with other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel enhancement techniques incorporating a smoothness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constraint in their level set functions [24, 25].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For an automated segmentation method used in screen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing, the most important properties are robustness, efficiency,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the calculation time, because hundreds or thousands of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images have to be processed each day. The state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel segmentation methods [12, 22] usually have high com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putational needs and achieve an accuracy of 90% to 94%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on eye-fundus images, with sensitivity of 60% to 70% and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specificity above 99% on average [26]. This is due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fact that approximately 85% of an image shows background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures. The high computational needs are due to multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis of large regions to detect thick vessels. 'Thus, the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putational needs of an algorithm is increasing exponentially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the diameter of the expected thickest vessel and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image resolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present an algorithm based on the vessel enhance-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment method published by Frangi et al. [1] in combination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a multiresolution framework to decrease the computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional needs and to increase the sensitivity by using a hystere-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sis thresholding. The method published by Frangi et al. [1] is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All methods that were used to analyze the images are des-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cribed in this section. First, we introduce the method pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed by Frangi et al. [1], which provides the basis of this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work. This is followed by the description of the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method: the preprocessing steps in Section 3.2.1 and the used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution hierarchy in Section 3.2.2. After that the vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancement method is described to highlight the main

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences to the Frangi method. We have chosen the method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: published by Frangi et al. [1] as a base for our own work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because it features some attractive properties.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (i) High accuracy is expected based on preliminary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research [1, 27]. For further information please see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 5.1. In comparison, our implementation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this method achieved a high accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (ii) No user interaction is required, except for setting a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few parameters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (iii) It is able to segment nonconnected objects without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complex initialization steps. This is necessary in case

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of some abnormalities and in case of young patients,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where reflections may disconnect vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: real vessels. Since the background pixels have a small mag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitude of derivatives and, thus; small eigenvalues, S helps to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinguish between noise and background.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The authors suggest to repeat the same calculations for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: varying sigma values from one to the thickest expected vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness with an increment of 1.0 to enhance vessels with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different thicknesses. The results are combined by a weighted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum projection. In our implementation we added a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding step after the combination and optimized the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters to reach the highest accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2. Proposed Method. After the preprocessing steps, we apply

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same equations as described by Frangi et al. [1] for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution level with the same predefined sigma value.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hence, we do not increase the sigma value linearly and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: apply the filter multiple times on the image as it was proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Frangi et al. [1]. In our case the sigma is always set to a small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constant, while we apply the same method on copies of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input image with reduced resolutions. Thus, the parameter s

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the original method corresponds to the resolution of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image, instead of the standard deviation of a Gaussian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The proposed algorithm of our method is illustrated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2. Each of the steps will be discussed in detail in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: next sections.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.1. Preprocessing. The input images are digital color fundus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: photographs like the one in Figure 1. During the analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we restrict ourselves to the green channel. It has the highest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast between the vessels and the background, while it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is not underilluminated or oversaturated like the other two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: channels, see Figure 3 for an example. Histogram stretching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [28] and bilateral filtering [29] are applied to the green chan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nel. The histogram stretching increases the contrast to make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it easier for the algorithm to detect small changes and distin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guish different tissues. The bilateral filtering [30] is a special

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denoising algorithm, which smooths intensity changes, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserving the boundaries of different regions or tissues. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: step reduces false positive detections caused by the texture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the background. After these modifications of the data, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can apply our resolution hierarchy described in the next sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.2. Resolution Hierarchy. In a resolution hierarchy copies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the input image with reduced resolutions are generated; see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 4. By doing so, we calculate the Hessian matrix always

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for a small neighborhood which decreases the computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: needs. The reduction is done by a subsampling followed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a low pass filtering to lower high jumps in intensities. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highest resolution level of the resolution hierarchy contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original image, and all additional levels contain the image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a halved width and height compared to the previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level. For low resolution images, where the vessel thickness is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not more than 5 to 10 pixels, 2 to 3 levels are sufficient, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images with higher resolutions may require additional levels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared to more than 20 iterations for the Frangi method,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this means a speedup of a factor of 10. The vessel enhancement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the Frangi algorithm is applied on each resolution level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a standard deviation σ = 1.0.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Sometimes the flash of the camera causes a shining cen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terline on thick vessels. An additional correction method was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: developed to remove these specular reflection artifacts in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduced resolution levels. The resulting images of the vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancement are resized again using bilinear interpolation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the same resolution as the input image. Figure 5 shows the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result of this resizing on two different resolution copies of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same region. Figure 5(a) had a high resolution and the result

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows finer details, but the thickest vessels are not enhanced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correctly. Figure 5(b) had a much lower resolution. Thus, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine details disappeared, but the extraction of thick vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were more accurate.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.3. Specular Reflex Correction. As mentioned before, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flash of the camera may cause a bright specular reflex in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the middle of thick vessels. Because of these reflections, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hessian-based filter will have a much lower response. In our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithm we developed a filter to be used on the highest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level of our resolution pyramid to reduce the effect of these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflections. In this level only thick vessels are detected. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consider a 3×3 neighborhood for each pixel. If the center pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a lower value than two neighboring pixels in opposite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directions in the vessel enhanced image, but higher value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the same two pixels in the fundus image of the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution level, then the center pixels are affected by specular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflex. In this case the two neighboring pixel's value will be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpolated to update the center pixel's value.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.4. Hysteresis Threshold. After the vessel enhancement is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completed in each resolution level and the results are resized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to original resolution, all of them are binarized by a threshold-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing algorithm proposed by Canny [31]. The method performs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better than a single thresholding in cases where the intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the objects is at some places high, but in certain positions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the contrast between object and background falls under noise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level. In our case this object is the vessel tree, where thin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels and boundary pixel intensities can have extreme low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity values. This method uses two thresholding values

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instead of one to binarize a gray-scale image. Both threshold

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values have different roles in the thresholding process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) The first threshold is used to determine pixels with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high intensities. It is required that this threshold is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chosen in such a way that no background pixel can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reach that value. Thus, we can label all the pixels above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the threshold as "vessel pixels."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) We label all pixels below the second threshold value as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "background pixel" and all pixels in between the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholds are considered “potential vessel pixels."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These potential vessel pixels are labeled as vessels only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: if they are connected to a pixel labeled “vessel pixel"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through other potential vessel pixels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The thresholding values are computed for each image that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a given percent of the pixels is segmented as “vessel pixels."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus, the binarization is more robust to noise and intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changes between images. 'They have to be optimized for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different protocol and field of view, where the ratio of vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and background pixels is different in the resulting image. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binarization is used on each image separately.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.5. Postprocessing. The final segmented image is generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by applying a pixel-wise OR operator on the binarized images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: originated from the different resolution levels. This way if a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel was detected in one of the images, then it will be visible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the combined binary image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We applied the original Frangi vesselness extraction and our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed framework on the commonly used DRIVE [26]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and STARE [32] databases and on our high resolution public

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: database [33] to compare our framework to the state-of-the-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: art methods and to evaluate their effectivity. These databases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contain manual segmentations of experts as gold standard.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on these gold standards we calculated the sensitivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Se), specificity (Sp), and accuracy (Acc) of each method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Both already existing databases contain an additional manual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation and the DRIVE database contains some mea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surements of multiple algorithms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We compare the computation time of the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithm and an implemented Frangi vesselness algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as proposed by Frangi et al. [1]. The two public databases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were used to evaluate the efficiency and for comparison

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to other state-of-the-art algorithms. These two databases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suffer from containing only low resolution images, while the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed method was developed for high resolution images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus, the benefit of the resolution hierarchy is only slightly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noticeable. Since high resolution images are becoming more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common in clinical use, we evaluated our methods on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high resolution (3504 × 2336 pixels) images available [33],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which were already used to evaluate other methods [6, 7].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The database contains 15 images of each healthy, diabetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinopathy (DR), and glaucomatous eyes. The results of this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation are discussed in Section 5.2.

layout_dets.text: 5. Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.1. Accuracy. The metrics calculated on the two public

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: databases to analyze the effectivity of the algorithms are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Tables 2 and 3. During our development and in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our comparisons we aimed at the highest possible accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, we optimized the parameters of both—the pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed and the Frangi—methods. 'Thus, the parameters of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Frangi method and the proposed method are set to deliver

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the highest possible accuracy. This can result in a decreased

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitivity to gain specificity in order to increase the overall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy. This way the proposed method was able to reach the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best accuracy using the DRIVE and high resolution fundus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: databases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: tation made by a human observer, which was included in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the comparison. We collected further results from published

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: papers. For both databases the original method and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 93%, respectively. As shown in Table 2, in case of the DRIVE

layout_dets.text: 7. Robustness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To analyze the robustness and sensitivity of the method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regarding changes in the parameters, we analyze it by further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excluding some steps and changing the parameters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As Table 8 shows, the algorithm is robust against changes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the parameters of pre- or postprocessing, except that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not all of the processing steps are skipped. This increases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the false positive values due to the appearance of small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmented noisy regions and also increases false negatives by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not segmenting regions of vessels with specular reflexes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The accuracy of the method improved surprisingly by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing the σ to 2.0 for the vessel enhancement. Our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis showed that the optimization using a small subset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of images resulted in a suboptimal parameter set for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whole dataset. Changing the sigma value to 2.0 increased the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitivity in multiple images, reaching an overall sensitivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over 0.7338 and accuracy over 0.9621.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8. Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our evaluation has shown that the proposed method not only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has the highest accuracy using the high resolution images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for which it was developed, but it has decent results using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two lower resolution databases available online. 'This decrease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is due to the slightly lower sensitivity caused by the lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image quality in the online databases. The proposed method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has lower computational needs compared to the method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed by Frangi et al. [1], as it was shown experimentally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Section 5.2 and mathematically proven in Section 6.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, as shown in Section 7, the method is only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slightly sensitive to the σ parameter of the vessel enhance-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment and the thresholding parameters. Changing σ can result

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 5% change in sensitivity, while changing most of the other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters resulted in a small variation in both sensitivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and specificity with an accuracy change under 0.1%.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 9. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper we presented a multiresolution method for seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: menting blood vessels in fundus photographs. 'The proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method and the Frangi method were evaluated using multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: online available databases with diverging image resolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The proposed algorithm shows in each case an increase both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in sensitivity and accuracy to segment vessels compared to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Frangi method with a decreased computational complex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This gain in accuracy is mainly due to easier handling of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: central reflexes of thick vessels in lower resolution images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while the computational needs are significantly reduced by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the resolution hierarchy. 'This can be further improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by parallelization and implementation using a GPU.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the proposed modifications the algorithm is more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applicable in complex automatic systems, and the segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation results can be used as a basis for other algorithms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to analyze abnormalities of the human eye. Additionally we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced a new high resolution fundus image database [33]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to evaluate segmentation and localization methods, where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our algorithm reached an accuracy of over 96% on average.
